step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identify visual nodes from the world model: three client S3 buckets (CLIENT 1, CLIENT 2, CLIENT N), a central S3 ACCESS LOGS bucket, a Lambda parsing function, an OpenSearch (ELASTICSEARCH) cluster running anomaly detection, and an SNS notification topic.
2. Map services to valid vocabulary: S3 -> S3, Lambda -> Lambda, ELASTICSEARCH -> OpenSearch, SNS -> SNS.
3. Assign sequential string IDs to nodes starting from '0'.
4. Map relationships and edge flows: S3 access logs flow from individual client buckets to S3 ACCESS LOGS. Log landing triggers Lambda function. Lambda enriches logs (GeoIP mapping, numeric country ID, client name) and pushes them to Elasticsearch. Elasticsearch anomaly detector evaluates access patterns and triggers SNS alerts upon anomaly detection.
